fields.summary: Autonomous plan run: no owner present. The planner read the intent, the daemon code (daemonPoll1, daemonNudge, session.StallAfter, inbox stalled items) and the overlapping queued bug requests 01M6W8KN, 01M6W9VN and 01M6WBVX, and raised four choices as one question for the arbiter: scope against those requests, stalled-step recovery, PR recovery and shipped defaults. The arbiter answered with Decision watchdog-scope-and-defaults: the watchdog is the daemon-level backstop that acts only on runs that stalled or ended on a transient signature, never while a step's own recovery is live, with its own per-run retry budget; stalled autonomous steps are nudged, then stopped and retried, while owner-attended runs get only a log line and an inbox item; a PR with no CI gets origin/main merged in and pushed normally (never rebase or force-push), a green unmerged PR gets its run resumed so the workflow merges it. The defaults are machine keys rhiza.daemon.watchdog.*, written as flat full-key strings under [daemon] in the root's rhiza.toml with camelCase names: agentNudge 20m then agentRetry 40m for agent steps, commandLimit 30m for command steps, waitLimit 90m for CI and PR waits, retryBudget 2, ciReruns 1 (once per PR head), pollBehind 3 (warn past 3x the interval), fileBugs true, autonomousOnly true, enabled true. Project keys rhiza.project.watchdog.* of the same names (all but pollBehind) in the project's git config override the machine keys. The change set serves milestone-25 (the daemon builds and ships the queued requests on its own), as its sibling requests do.
fields.title: Daemon watchdog plan, autonomous interview with the arbiter

set.statement: The daemon resumes an interrupted run whose change set is accepted, or whose change set has landed when it is a plan-workflow run (daemon-resumes-landed-plan-run) or a non-plan run whose journal reached its land step (daemon-resumes-landed-past-land), once, as a detached rhiza run resume --foreground <run> process outside Rex (daemon-headless-run-drivers), and journals that resume in the run's journal; it leaves alone every other interrupted run whose change set is not accepted. A run interrupted again after that resume, and every failed run, gets no second plain resume: it is left to the watchdog's policy (daemon-watchdog and its leaves), which may resume it with --retry within the per-run retry budget; only when that policy does not apply, is turned off in rhiza.toml, or its budget is spent does the run stay listed in the inbox as a run the daemon gave up on, or as failed.
